questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Identify the part of a neuron that receives signals
questions.stem: During handover, the nurse notes a neuron's signal-receiving projections are its dendrites.

options.text: Dendrites collect incoming signals from other neurons
Axon terminals collect incoming signals from other neurons
The soma collects all incoming signals exclusively
options.misconception: overstates the cell body receiving role

options.text: Myelin collects incoming signals from other neurons

questions.explanation: Dendrites are the input structures of a neuron. Axon terminals release neurotransmitters instead. The soma integrates but does not exclusively receive, and myelin insulates rather than receives.
questions.hint: Think about which part faces other neurons.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.stem: A nurse describes saltatory conduction jumping between nodes of Ranvier.

options.text: Myelin generates new action potentials at every segment
Myelin insulates axons so action potentials leap between gaps

Nodes of Ranvier are the myelin itself

questions.explanation: Myelin insulates the axon, forcing current to jump between nodes of Ranvier. It does not generate potentials, slow conduction, or constitute the nodes themselves.
questions.hint: Insulation forces the signal to skip.
